children.text: A viewpoint in the Busay hills north of Cebu City, about 600 m above sea level, looking out over the city, the Mactan Channel and the bridge. Rebuilt as a complex with a hexagon-paved plaza, restaurants and a rooftop deck, it is popular for its evening afterglow and night views.
Tops Lookout is a viewing spot on a ridge in the Busay foothills north of Cebu City, at about
above sea level. It is not far from the city center as the crow flies, but you have to climb about
10 km

of winding hill road, and in return all of Metro Cebu fits in one frame. The skyscrapers and port, the Cebu–Cordova Link Expressway (CCLEX) across the Mactan Channel, and Mactan Island itself are all in view, and on a clear day the horizon is said to reach all the way to Bohol across the sea.
The history goes back to
. Opened by Lito Osmeña, who later became governor of Cebu, it was a modest hilltop retreat with stone shelters, benches and stone arches, and for about
37 years
it welcomed couples, families and night-drive visitors. It then closed for a large-scale redevelopment and held a soft reopening in
February 2024

; today it is a complex called "The Circle at TOPS." A five-storey building curves around a round plaza and houses restaurants, cafés and small shops, and on the roof is the SKAI 360° deck, which charges a separate fee.

The stone arches and hexagonal paving stones that hold memories of the old days are still there and blend in with the new building. Walk along the railing at the edge of the plaza and Cebu City spreads out in front of you. The lookout faces southeast down over the city, so the sun does not set into the sea, but after sunset the afterglow spreads over the water and sky and the city lights come on one by one, all from the same spot. The entrance is open
24 hours
and some people go up for sunrise, but the restaurant area usually operates from
10 AM
to
11 PM

This guide covers a place where you can enjoy the view, the plaza and the food all at once: an evening hilltop night-view course. It suits travelers who finish sightseeing in the city (Magellan's Cross, the Santo Niño Basilica) and come up in the evening for night views and dinner, travelers bringing family or parents who want an easy view, and couples looking for a romantic evening. There is almost no walking or climbing, so it is easy on the legs, but planning for clear weather and your transport in advance makes a big difference to how much you enjoy it.

blocks.title: Afterglow and night views in one visit

children.text: Sunset falls roughly between 5:30 PM and 6:20 PM depending on the season. Arrive
30 minutes to 1 hour

before sunset, take a spot at the railing, and watch the sky change color and the city lights switch on one after another. For night photos, resting your elbows on the railing reduces shake even without a tripod.
This is the deck on the roof of the building above the plaza, and it costs about

extra on top of admission. The view is higher than from the plaza, so you can see the hills and the sea without obstruction, and the breeze is cool. Evenings can mean a wait, so it is better to go up before sunset.

blocks.title: Hexagonal paving and the stone-arch plaza

children.text: The hexagonal paved floor and round stone arches, symbols carried over from the old Tops, are still a favorite photo spot. Stand between the successive arches and shoot inward for a composition with depth, and at night, when the lights are on, the texture of the stone looks even sharper.

blocks.title: City and channel on a clear day

children.text: The view is worth seeing in the daytime too, not just at night. On a dry-season morning the city buildings, the bridge over the Mactan Channel and the outlines of distant islands are crisp. A coin-operated telescope also lets you zoom in on the city skyline.

On many days singers perform acoustic sets on one side of the plaza, and there are open-air seats on the ground floor of the shopping building and around the edge of the plaza. With more than 15 restaurants and cafés serving Filipino grilled dishes, Japanese food, pizza, burgers and gelato, you can eat while looking at the view.

In one corner of the viewing area stand wire sculptures of figures in skirts, covered with colorful padlocks. Couples hang love locks here, and at night the lights come on and make for a different kind of photo.

The entrance is open around the clock, so some visitors come up at sunrise. The restaurant area is not yet open then, so bring food and water and book your ride down in advance. It suits anyone who wants the quiet morning air and to watch the city wake up.
Restaurants and cafés with good views line the Busay road around Tops as well. You can stop by on the way down after the night view, or go up early and wait for sunset over a cup of tea.

In the rainy season clouds and fog are common during the day, so early morning gives the best visibility.
This is the easiest way. The drive from IT Park in Cebu City to Tops takes about
20–40 minutes
, and a one-way fare is about

from IT Park or JY Square, though drivers may ask close to ₱1,000 from the city center. Cars can be scarce when you come back down, so negotiate a round trip with waiting time or book one on the app before you leave.
A shuttle to Tops runs from the Cebu IT Park transport terminal. The round-trip fare including admission is about
and the ride takes about
20 minutes
. It generally runs from
7 AM
until
2–3 AM
, but this changes with the season and announcements, so check the schedule on site.
Habal-habal climb the hill from around JY Square (Lahug). Negotiate about
one way per person, and since the road is steep with many sharp curves, ask for a helmet and a safe ride.
Enter "Tops Cebu" or "Cebu Tops Road" into your navigation. There is a parking lot, and parking costs about
(about ₱30 for motorbikes). The road up is steep, so check your brakes and drive slowly.
First fly into Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB). There are direct flights from Korea, and from Manila it takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
. From the airport to Tops takes about
1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes
by car, so most people drop their bags at a hotel in the city and head up in the evening.
During the dry season from
December
to
May
the sky is clear and the city and distant sea are at their sharpest. The hill is about
above sea level, so it is roughly
cooler than the city, and in the evening the wind makes it feel fresh. In the
June–November
rainy season, clouds and fog are frequent and visibility drops, and the hill road can be dangerous when a typhoon warning is issued.
Around the Sinulog Festival in the third week of
January

, the Christmas and New Year holidays and Holy Week, local families crowd the place. Choose a weekday or arrive well before sunset to claim a spot. The view faces the sea to the east, so some people also come around sunrise at
, but the restaurant area is closed and transport is limited then, so an evening visit is far more common.
During the day,
is when city buildings and the sea show their clearest colors, while
12 noon to 3 PM
has strong sun that washes the sky out white and is quite hot.
5 to 6:30 PM
is the most popular window, when the afterglow runs into the night view, and after
8 PM

crowds thin out and you can enjoy the lights in peace. Right after rain the air is washed clean and the night view is especially sharp, so an evening after a shower can actually be a good opportunity.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Dry season. Clear, transparent air gives the longest view
Best for afterglow and night views. Weekends around the January Sinulog Festival are very crowded
Rainy season. Frequent showers, fog and clouds
Often hazy. Aim for the morning or an evening after the rain
End of the rainy season. Typhoon effects and on-and-off rain
Postpone if a typhoon warning is up. Some evenings after rain give a sharp night view

items.label: Admission
items.note: Seniors and persons with disabilities ₱70, bring cash

items.label: Grab or taxi one way
items.note: Drivers may ask close to ₱1,000 from the city center

children.text: Prices are rough estimates as of 2026 and may vary with local conditions.

There is no accommodation at Tops itself, and most people stay in downtown Cebu (around IT Park and Ayala Center Cebu) or on Mactan Island and come up in the evening. Around IT Park, mid-range hotels run roughly ₱2,000–4,000 and upscale hotels roughly ₱5,000 and up (varying a lot by season), and Lahug and Busay also have boutique stays and Airbnbs with good views. If you want to spend a night on the hill, look for a view stay in Busay, but public transport is poor, so secure your own way to get around.

The plaza restaurants have more than 15 shops, from Filipino grilled dishes (inihaw), Japanese izakaya and ramen to pizza and burgers, steak, gelato, tapioca drinks and matcha desserts. A main dish runs roughly ₱250–500 and a drink roughly ₱100–200, varying by shop. Prices are somewhat higher than at lowland malls. If you want a more atmospheric meal than the plaza offers, you can also find the viewpoint restaurants and cafés along the Busay road and enjoy the scenery over a cup of tea before sunset.
The entrance is open 24 hours so you can catch sunrise, but the restaurants only open from about 10 AM to 11 PM. Assume there is nowhere to eat in the early morning or late at night.

If you arrive between 4:30 and 5 PM on a clear day, you can see both the afterglow hours and the night view. On days when low clouds hang over the city it may not be visible, so check the sky that day.
At about 600 m above sea level it is windier and chillier than in the city. Bring a thin windbreaker or a light jacket.
The parking lot and the plaza entrance get congested at the evening peak, so going up by shuttle or Grab is easier. If you bring a car, go up early, before sunset.
Cash is easier for tickets. Bring plenty of small bills (₱100, ₱50).
Going up by shuttle is easy, but cars can pile up on the way down, so check the last shuttle time in advance and set a time to head down.
For night photos, steady your camera or phone on the railing and use night mode and a timer for sharp shots.
Saturday, Sunday and holiday evenings are very crowded with local families. For a relaxed visit, weekday evenings or early afternoon are recommended.
The SKAI 360° rooftop deck may operate differently depending on weather or maintenance, so check at the entrance before going up.

Admission fees, shuttle hours and rooftop deck operations can change without notice. Tops has been operating normally in 2026, after the earthquake in northern Cebu in late September 2025, but check the latest announcements before you go.
The Busay hill road has many steep slopes and sharp curves and is slippery in the rainy season. When riding a habal-habal, wear a helmet and ask the driver not to speed.
Some visitors get stuck at night with no ride down. Arrange a round trip with waiting time or the last shuttle in advance.
On days with heavy rain or a typhoon warning, there is a risk of landslides and road closures, so postpone your visit.
The slope beyond the railing and the edges of the stairs are dark. Hold children's hands when you bring them.
When it is crowded, carry your phone and bag in front, and do not put your things down in a corner of the plaza while you take photos.
